transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’ve been thinking about death a lot lately, and wondering if my family would just be better off without me. I confided in my daughter about it recently, and she got so worried that she insisted on bringing me in to get some help.

Before this current period, have you ever had another episode lasting at least two weeks when you felt similarly depressed or lost interest in things? If so, about how many separate episodes have you had?

I’m not really sure, and I don't recall having separate, distinct episodes before this past year. My struggles with these mood swings and deep depressions have mostly just been coming and going over the last year since I started transitioning into retirement.

When you’re feeling most depressed, have you had any experiences like hearing or seeing things others don’t, or strongly believing something that others say isn’t true? Even if it feels hard to talk about, this would help me understand what you’re going through.

No, I've never experienced anything like that. I haven't heard or seen things that aren't there, nor have I held any beliefs that others found completely untrue or bizarre, even at my absolute lowest.

Have you ever had a period lasting several days or longer when you felt unusually energetic or euphoric, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or felt your thoughts were racing? Even if it didn’t seem like a problem at the time, has anything like that ever happened?

Yes, a few weeks ago I had a stretch where I felt incredibly wired, upbeat, and touchy all at once, talking a mile a minute with racing thoughts that made it hard to sleep. I was up before dawn cleaning, taking on way too many volunteer projects, and feeling like I was the only one who could fix things. Looking back, it feels a bit over-the-top, but at the time I just couldn't slow down.

During that high-energy period, did it get so severe that you needed to be hospitalized or it caused major problems at work, finances, relationships, or legal trouble? Also, did you have any psychotic symptoms then, like hearing things or having beliefs others said weren’t true?

No, I was never hospitalized, and I didn't have legal trouble or hear voices, though I did have those over-the-top thoughts about being the only one who could fix our condo community. It did cause some strain because I overcommitted to way too many projects at once and couldn't keep up. I even almost invested a large chunk of our savings into an eco-housing project I saw online before my daughter talked me down.
